symbols.note: Assembles inventory document dict from render reports and annotations; writes nothing.

claims.text: Derive the whole document. Writes nothing.
claims.why: The function body in this chunk only constructs a dict and returns it; no filesystem writes are present.

claims.text: reports is the (reach, switches) pair from daedalus.mapping.render.analyse_once. When it is not supplied this calls that function -- which is the configuration the PRODUCT uses, index and all.
claims.why: The code uses `reports or render_mod.analyse_once(root, index)` and imports render_mod from .render, matching the claim.

claims.text: Calling reach.analyse(root) with no index here would be a second engine configuration that ships to nobody, and the last time a guard did that a CRITICAL survived underneath it.
claims.why: The chunk does not call reach.analyse directly; the claim refers to historical context outside this chunk.

claims.text: Reported, NOT filed as a stale feature. Its remedy is 'add it to the list', the exact opposite verb from the stale remedy ('remove it'), and handing a fixer the wrong verb is how a finding becomes damage.
claims.why: The code places on_disk_but_unlisted under packaging and does not add it to stale_features; ghosts are added as stale features with detector 'packaging_ghost'.

claims.text: The count that cannot be lowered by deleting a test.
claims.why: The code computes 'unreached' as len(set(islands) | set(shims) | set(unknown)) and later as sorted union, which is robust to moving modules between island/unknown by deleting tests.

claims.text: The prose summaries the previous schema carried. Derived from the SAME pass as the structured features, so the discrepancy the picker reports when the two disagree cannot occur by construction.
claims.why: The keys islands, shims, unknown, unreached, stale are derived from the same grouped/status data in this function, not from a separate pass.

claims.text: unreached is here because the island COUNT is gameable and was demonstrated to be: 'island' means unreachable but imported by a test, so deleting the test moves the module to unknown and the island count goes DOWN while the dead code stays. The union is the number that cannot be improved by deleting a test, and the set diff against the previous run is the honest signal -- not the count.
claims.why: The code uses the union of islands, shims, and unknown for 'unreached', which cannot decrease by moving a module from island to unknown; the rationale matches.

claims.text: Regenerate in place, carrying the human half forward. The old document is read for its annotations BEFORE it is overwritten, and a first run over a schema-1 file harvests them out of the hand-written entries. Refreshing is never a way to quietly drop somebody's stated reason.
claims.why: The chunk shows reading old via load() and calling harvest(), but the actual overwrite and harvest logic are in later lines not present; cannot verify the full claim.

observations.what: Packaging ghost features are always created with 'tests': [] even if annotations or other sources might provide test provenance.
refresh() silently discards old annotations if the file is corrupt (load returns {'__error__': ...}) by setting old = {}.
build() uses `reports or render_mod.analyse_once(...)`; if reports is an empty tuple (falsy), it will re-run analysis even though a (possibly intentionally empty) report was passed.
The docstring claim about PRODUCT configuration is not verifiable within this chunk; it depends on render.analyse_once usage elsewhere.
